Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions will be provided at that time for queuing questions using the dial-in method. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q2 2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid second quarter, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us on our second quarter 2024 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as we're known. I'll walk you through our financial results, which once again demonstrate the resilience and strength of our portfolio amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment, and then share our outlook for the balance of the year. As always, all figures I reference are on an adjusted, continuing operations basis unless otherwise noted, and we've reconciled these to GAAP in our press release and 10-Q filing.

Starting with the top line: Q2 net sales reached $18.7 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year, or 5.8% on an organic basis. This marks our sixth straight quarter of positive organic growth, driven by a healthy mix of 2.1% volume/mix expansion and 3.7% pricing actions. Volume growth was particularly encouraging, reflecting share gains across premium segments despite softer category trends in mass-market staples. Pricing remained disciplined, focused on recovering input cost inflation—think soybean oil, PET resin, and energy surcharges—while protecting consumer value through targeted promotions.

Breaking it down by segment, our Beauty & Personal Care division, home to powerhouse brands like Lumina shampoo and VitalGlow skincare, delivered organic growth of 7.2%, fueled by 4% volume uplift from our prestige haircare launches and e-commerce penetration now at 28% of divisional sales, up from 22% last year. Health & Wellness, including our probiotic yogurts under NutriCore and plant-based alternatives akin to Chobani’s expansions, grew 6.5% organically, with double-digit gains in emerging markets from RTD protein shakes. Fabric & Home Care—think UltraClean detergents and FreshWave air care—saw 4.8% organic growth, bolstered by sustainability-driven innovations like our 100% recyclable bottle formats, which captured 15% market share in North America per Nielsen data. Nutrition rounded out at 3.9% organic, where we lapped tough comps from last year’s supply disruptions but stabilized volumes through localized sourcing in snacks and beverages.

Gross margin expanded 210 basis points to 53.4%, our highest in five years, thanks to a multi-year productivity program yielding $450 million in savings this quarter alone. Key levers included supply chain optimization via our AI-powered demand sensing platform—now covering 85% of our SKUs—which reduced inventory days by 12 to 68 days and cut stockouts by 30%. We also accelerated supplier negotiations post the Red Sea disruptions, locking in forward contracts for 70% of 2025 pulp needs at favorable rates. Core operating margin hit 22.1%, up 140 bps, as SG&A leverage improved to 30.7% of sales from disciplined media spend—ROI now averaging 4.2x across digital channels—and zero-based budgeting that trimmed overhead by 8%.

Adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.42, up 11% year-over-year and 8% ex-currency, beating our whisper number and reflecting $0.05 from share repurchases under our $5 billion authorization—we bought back 1.2% of shares outstanding this quarter. Free cash flow was robust at $2.1 billion, or 11% of sales, supporting a dividend increase to $0.78 per share, our 28th consecutive hike. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA stands at a healthy 2.1x, giving us ample dry powder for bolt-on M&A like our recent $1.2 billion acquisition of EcoFresh, a clean-label condiment player expanding our position in the $25 billion global sauces category.

Regionally, North America contributed 48% of sales with 5.1% organic growth, driven by premiumization—consumers trading up to our $10+ haircare lines amid 3.5% category inflation per IRI data—though pantry-loading slowed post-holiday. Europe, at 28% of sales, grew 4.9% organically despite regulatory headwinds on PFAS in packaging; we gained 90 bps share in UK laundry via our enzyme-boosted EcoWash pods. Emerging markets, our growth engine at 24% of sales, surged 8.3% organically: Latin America up 11% on volume recovery in Brazil snacks, Asia-Pacific 7% with China beauty e-commerce via Tmall doubling to $400 million annualized run-rate, and India’s affordable nutrition packs adding 150 bps share per Kantar.

Now, turning to outlook. For the full year 2024, we’re raising guidance across the board. Organic sales growth now expected at 4.5% to 5.5%, up from 4% to 5%, reflecting stronger-than-anticipated volume momentum and pricing normalization. Adjusted EPS guidance lifted to $5.65 to $5.80, a 9% to 12% increase at midpoint, incorporating $1.1 billion in productivity savings offset by $300 million in strategic investments—namely, $150 million in U.S. direct-to-consumer platforms and $100 million in regenerative agriculture for cocoa and palm supply chains to meet EU deforestation regs.

I'll now turn to our gross margin outlook, which remains a cornerstone of our profitability story here at GCB. As we discussed in our Q2 pre-announcement, we're reaffirming our full-year fiscal 2024 gross margin guidance at 45.5% to 46.5%, representing approximately 130 to 180 basis points of expansion versus our FY23 adjusted gross margin of 44.2%. This guidance embeds a sequential step-up from Q3's expected 45.8% to Q4's 46.2% midpoint, driven by the continued unwind of last year's cocoa and palm oil shock, layered with our structural productivity gains.

Let me unpack the key assumptions underpinning this outlook, starting with the puts and takes. On the cost side, input cost inflation remains the elephant in the room for CPG, much like it was industry-wide in 2023 when cocoa futures spiked over 150% year-over-year amid West African supply disruptions. We've seen some moderation—cocoa prices are down 25% from their March peak—but we still assume a net 3-5% YoY input cost headwind in FY24, primarily from lingering effects in chocolate coatings for our SnackJoy bar line and palm oil derivatives in household cleaners. That said, our hedging program covers 70% of our FY24 cocoa needs at favorable rates below $4,000 per ton, mitigating roughly $150 million in potential exposure. For palm oil, we're 50% hedged, with sustainability-linked contracts from RSPO-certified suppliers helping to stabilize pricing at around 1,100 MYR per ton.

Offsetting this, pricing actions continue to deliver robust tailwinds. We've embedded 5-7% net price realization across our portfolio, with particular strength in North America where we've taken two waves of pricing on our flagship PowerQuench hydration beverages—up 8% list, netting 6% after trade spend optimization. In EMEA, pricing is at 6% amid softer consumer sentiment, but we've protected margins by accelerating private label exits in low-margin laundry pods, redirecting capacity to premium EcoClean lines. APAC is our bright spot, with 9% pricing on health & wellness SKUs like our new PlantVita protein snacks, fueled by premiumization trends in China and India. Overall, these actions should contribute 250 basis points of margin expansion, echoing the playbook that helped peers like Mondelez and Hershey rebuild margins post-inflation.

Productivity is the real margin accelerator here, and we're on track for $250 million in gross savings for the year—up from $180 million in FY23—through our "MarginMax" initiative. This includes $100 million from supply chain digitization, like AI-driven demand sensing in our SAP S/4HANA platform, which has reduced inventory obsolescence by 15% in our beverage plants and cut logistics costs 8% via dynamic routing with partners like Maersk. We've also rolled out robotic process automation (RPA) in 12 facilities, targeting a 20% reduction in variable conversion costs for snacks production—think precision dosing for nut inclusions to minimize waste. On the sourcing front, our regenerative agriculture program with suppliers in Brazil for coffee and soy has yielded a 5% cost avoidance through yield improvements, aligning with our sustainability commitments and ahead of Unilever's similar efforts.

Regionally, North America drives 60% of our expansion, with gross margins expected at 48%, benefiting from favorable dairy and corn futures and our shift to higher-margin RTD coffee pods, where we're gaining share versus Keurig Dr Pepper. EMEA faces a 2% input drag from energy passthroughs but still expands 100 bps to 44% via optimized pack sizes and e-commerce fulfillment efficiencies. Emerging markets, at 42% margins, get a lift from local-for-local manufacturing in Southeast Asia, reducing FX volatility impacts—we assume a neutral $0.02 headwind from USD strength against the euro and real.

Strategically, this guidance reflects our disciplined portfolio management: we're divesting two low-margin legacy brands in pet food, representing 2% of sales but only 1% of gross profit, to fund innovation in high-growth adjacencies like functional beverages and clean-label personal care. We're also leaning into consumer trends—health, sustainability, convenience—with 25% of new product launches in categories boasting 50%+ gross margins, similar to how PepsiCo's Poppi acquisition boosted their mix.

Of course, this is forward-looking and subject to risks like prolonged commodity volatility—say, if El Niño exacerbates palm yields—or weaker-than-expected volume resilience amid tariff talks. But with our balance sheet fortress, $1.2 billion in cash, and proven pricing power, we're confident in delivering the upper half of this range, positioning GCB for sustained 15%+ operating margins in FY25.

As we wrap up these financial details, I'd like to dive deeper into our four key strategic priorities, where we're making measurable progress amid a dynamic CPG landscape. Inflationary pressures persist—with U.S. CPI for food and beverages still hovering around 4-5% YoY per BLS data—but we're outperforming the category through disciplined pricing, innovation, and execution. Our total revenue grew 7.2% organically, outpacing the 3.1% Nielsen-measured CPG industry growth, driven by these pillars.

First, premiumization and health & wellness portfolio transformation. We're laser-focused on shifting our mix toward higher-margin premium SKUs, targeting health, wellness, and indulgence segments where consumers are trading up despite economic headwinds. We've divested three low-single-digit margin legacy brands—like our regional snack lines—for $450 million in proceeds, redeployed into bolt-on acquisitions such as the $1.2 billion purchase of VitaGlow, a plant-based personal care leader akin to Burt's Bees. Progress metrics are strong: Premium products now represent 42% of our portfolio revenue, up from 32% two years ago, delivering 250 bps of gross margin expansion to 48.7%. In beverages, our new "PureThrive" functional water line—infused with electrolytes and adaptogens—achieved 18% market share in the enhanced hydration subcategory within six months, per IRI data, outpacing competitors like PepsiCo's Gatorade Organic. Health & wellness velocity is up 12% in North America, with AURs averaging $3.25 versus $2.10 for mass-market peers. Looking ahead, we're targeting 50% premium mix by FY25, fueling 2-3% annual organic growth.

Second, accelerating digital and omnichannel growth. E-commerce has been our brightest spot, now 28% of total sales—up from 18% pre-pandemic—amid Amazon's dominance and the rise of DTC platforms. We've invested $250 million in our "NovaConnect" tech stack, including AI-driven personalization engines similar to Unilever's ecosystem, enabling hyper-targeted marketing with 35% higher conversion rates. Regionally, North America e-com grew 22% YoY to $1.8 billion, capturing 15% share in grocery DTC via partnerships with Instacart and Walmart+. In Europe, we're gaining traction post-Brexit with localized apps, hitting 20% penetration in the UK household care category. APAC is the wildcard: China e-com surged 45% to RMB 2.5 billion, driven by Tmall and JD.com listings for our "EcoFresh" cleaning pods, which boast 92% ACV distribution. We've also launched 15 DTC microsites, generating $150 million in direct sales with 40% repeat purchase rates. This pillar is expected to contribute 4-5 points of our FY24 growth, with ROIC exceeding 25%.

Third, sustainability and supply chain resilience. ESG isn't a buzzword—it's a competitive moat. Our "GreenCore" initiative aligns with SBTi net-zero goals by 2040, with 65% of packaging now recyclable or reusable, ahead of P&G's 2030 target. We've converted 80% of our North American supply chain to renewable energy, reducing Scope 2 emissions 28% YoY. Key progress: Sourced 45% of agricultural inputs—cocoa, palm oil, coffee—via regenerative farming, cutting water usage 22% per ton versus industry baselines from the World Resources Institute. This drove $180 million in cost avoidance from efficiency gains, including a 15% reduction in logistics costs via our Mexico City hub consolidation. In Latin America, Brazil volumes rebounded 11% post-droughts thanks to diversified sourcing from Colombia and Peru. Disruptions like Red Sea shipping delays added just 50 bps to COGS, versus 200 bps for peers per McKinsey CPG reports. We're on track for 75% sustainable sourcing by 2025, enhancing brand loyalty—NPS scores up 8 points to 72 in eco-focused surveys.

Fourth, category leadership and geographic expansion. We're doubling down on core power brands—laundry (25% market share), snacks (18%), and beverages (22%)—while expanding into high-growth regions. In snacks, our "CrunchVital" protein bars gained 4 points of share in the U.S., hitting 15% in IRI's health bar tracker, fueled by 9% distribution gains to 95% ACV. Geographically, North America remains 55% of sales but grew 6% organically. Europe was flat at 2% amid soft demand, offset by 5% pricing. The star is Emerging Markets: APAC revenues up 15% to $2.4 billion, led by India where our affordable "DailyEssentials" pack hygiene products captured 12% share in a market growing 10% per Euromonitor. LatAm grew 12%, with Mexico laundry pods up 20% on premiumization. We've entered five new ASEAN markets via JVs, targeting $500 million incremental revenue by FY26.

These priorities position us for sustained outperformance: FY24 organic growth of 6-8%, mid-teens EPS expansion, and free cash flow of $3.2-3.5 billion. Risks like commodity volatility—cocoa up 40% YTD—and FX in EMs are mitigated by hedging 85% of exposures. We're executing with precision, much like Colgate's playbook in oral care, to deliver long-term TSR in the mid-20s percentile.

I'll now turn to the competitive landscape and our strategic responses, which continue to shape our performance across the CPG portfolio. As you know, the industry remains fiercely contested, with ACV share battles intensifying amid persistent inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and the relentless push toward premiumization and sustainability. Nielsen and IRI data for Q2 underscore this: category dollar growth slowed to just 2.1% YoY globally, down from 4.5% last year, driven by private label gains and promotional fatigue. But our proactive playbook—rooted in data analytics, agile innovation, and targeted trade investments—enabled us to defend 98% of our core market share while accelerating growth in high-margin segments.

In North America, which represents 45% of our revenue, we faced heightened aggression from Procter & Gamble on laundry detergents and Unilever in personal care. P&G's Tide Pods launched a mid-tier value pack at 15% below their premium ASP, capturing 1.8 points of ACV share in the liquid/pod segment per IRI scans—particularly among value-conscious households hit by grocery inflation averaging 3.2%. Unilever countered with Dove's "Clean Glow" line, emphasizing 100% recycled packaging, which boosted their facial skincare velocity by 4% in drug channels.

Our response was swift and surgical. We optimized pricing elasticity models using AI-driven tools from our partnership with Palantir, dynamically adjusting FreshGlow laundry promotions to maintain a 22% household penetration rate. This included a 12-week "Buy 2, Get 1 Half-Off" blitz in Walmart and Kroger, recapturing 1.2 share points and lifting our laundry category velocity 5% above category average. Trade spend rose modestly to 18% of CPG SG&A—up 200 bps QoQ—but ROI exceeded 3.5x, preserving 250 bps of gross margin. Result? Our NA CPG market share held steady at 27.8%, with premium pods growing 11% YoY versus flat category.

Europe, at 30% of sales, grappled with EU Green Deal mandates and discounter dominance. Reckitt's Dettol aggressively expanded eco-claims on disinfectants, gaining 2.5% share in household cleaners amid a 7% category contraction from inflation-weary shoppers. Aldi and Lidl private labels surged 14% in snacks, pressuring our SnackJoy portfolio.

We leaned into our "Planet Positive" platform, accelerating technical initiatives like bio-based surfactants in our EcoFresh cleaners—now 40% of the lineup—which met EU biodegradability thresholds ahead of 2025 regs. This drove a 9% uplift in e-commerce velocity on platforms like Ocado and Amazon, where we gained 3 points of digital share. Regionally, we shifted 15% of trade dollars to precision marketing via Kantar Worldpanel data, targeting Gen Z with TikTok AR try-ons for personal care. Outcome: European share dipped just 0.5 points to 24.2%, but sustainable SKUs grew 22% YoY, adding 80 bps to mix-driven margins.

In EMs—25% of revenue and our highest-growth engine—local players like India's Hindustan Unilever and Brazil's Natura ramped up. HUL's Rin detergent undercut us by 20% in rural channels, eroding 1.1 share points in mass laundry per Kantar data. Natura's clean beauty push in LATAM snagged 4% in facial care amid a premiumization trend where consumers traded up 6% despite 8-10% inflation.

Our counter? Hyper-local innovation and supply chain resilience. We rolled out 12 new "Affordable Premium" packs for SnackJoy—smaller 50g formats at 10% premium pricing—boosting distribution to 1.2 million incremental outlets in India and Indonesia. Leveraging our ASEAN manufacturing hubs, we cut logistics costs 7% via SAP-integrated forecasting, enabling competitive everyday low pricing. Digital went big: We invested $25M in JioMart and Shopee partnerships, driving 35% DTC growth and 2x velocity in urban millennials. Net result: EM share expanded 1.4 points to 19.6%, with volume up 8% despite FX headwinds.

Across regions, trends like health & wellness (now 28% of new product pipelines) and omnichannel velocity are pivotal. Competitors like PepsiCo are doubling down on hydration functionals, but our R&D spend—up 12% to 3.8% of sales—fuels 25 launches in FY24, including protein-fortified snacks targeting the $50B global wellness boom. We're also piloting blockchain traceability for supply chain transparency, countering Unilever's sustainability lead. Risks persist: If inflation eases slower than our 2-3% forecast, private labels could claim another 1-2 share points. But our $500M productivity program—spanning zero-based budgeting and GenAI for demand sensing—positions us to outpace. We expect FY24 CPG organic growth of 5-6%, with share gains in 7 of 10 core categories.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We saw strong performance in our SnackJoy and PowerQuench brands this quarter. As we dive into our financial results, I want to spend some time on a critical driver of our top-line growth: marketing campaign effectiveness. In the hyper-competitive CPG landscape—where we're battling giants like Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and PepsiCo for every share of wallet—our marketing investments delivered exceptional returns this quarter, underscoring the strength of our data-driven, omnichannel approach. Let me break this down with specifics on ROI metrics, campaign highlights, regional nuances, technical innovations, and forward-looking strategies.

First, the big picture. We allocated $285 million to marketing in Q2, representing 12.5% of net sales and up 8% year-over-year, in line with our disciplined AOR—advertising-to-sales ratio—target of 11-13%. This spend mix shifted further toward high-efficiency channels: 62% digital (up from 55% last year), 25% trade promotions via retail media networks (RMNs), 10% experiential and influencer, and just 3% traditional linear TV. The payoff? Our blended return on ad spend (ROAS) hit 4.7x, a 24% improvement from 3.8x in Q2 2023 and ahead of our internal benchmark of 4.0x. This was validated through our proprietary Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) framework, which incorporates econometrics, incrementality lift studies, and multi-touch attribution to isolate true causal impact—eliminating the fluff that plagues legacy CPG measurement.

Driving this were two flagship campaigns: our "Pure Bliss" relaunch for our Heritage Dairy yogurt line and the "Thrive Summer" activation across our plant-based protein snacks, inspired by the category surges seen with Beyond Meat and Chobani.

The "Pure Bliss" campaign targeted lapsed households in the $10B U.S. spoonable yogurt segment, where private label erosion has pressured incumbents like Danone. We deployed a $45M blitz: 40% on CTV and YouTube via programmatic buys optimized by our AI-powered demand-side platform (DSP), 30% on Amazon DSP and Walmart Connect RMNs for closed-loop attribution, 20% on TikTok Shop live streams with micro-influencers (average 50K followers, 15% engagement rate), and 10% on in-store sampling tied to loyalty apps. Results were stellar: a 28% lift in household penetration (measured via IRI syndicated data), 22% sales uplift to $165M (vs. flat category), and a campaign ROAS of 5.8x. Notably, incrementality testing via geo-holdout experiments showed 65% of sales were truly incremental—not just accelerated buys. Customer acquisition cost (CAC) dropped 18% to $4.20 per new household, boosting our CLV-to-CAC ratio to 3.8x, well above the CPG industry average of 2.5x per Nielsen benchmarks.

"Thrive Summer" leaned into the $5.5B plant-based snack boom, amid 12% category growth per SPINS data. With $38M invested, we focused on Gen Z and millennial parents via user-generated content (UGC) challenges on Instagram Reels and Snapchat, partnered with 250 nano-influencers (e.g., fitness creators akin to those boosting Kind Snacks). Digital dominated at 70% of spend, with Shopify-powered DTC pop-ups contributing 15% of volume. Outcomes: 35% awareness lift (per Kantar tracking), 19% market share gain to 14.2% in the segment, and ROAS of 6.2x—the highest in our portfolio. A/B testing on creative variants revealed sustainability messaging (e.g., "carbon-neutral sourcing") outperformed fun/flavor by 40% in conversion rates, informing our ESG-linked strategy.

Regionally, performance varied but stayed robust, reflecting tailored localization amid divergent market dynamics. In North America (65% of our marketing spend, $185M), ROAS was 5.1x, fueled by RMN dominance—Walmart Connect and Kroger Precision Marketing delivered 7.2x ROAS on $42M, capturing 1st-party data goldmines post-cookie deprecation. Trade promo efficiency hit 3.5x, with promo price elasticity at -2.8 (better than Unilever's reported -3.2), minimizing elasticities from inflation-weary shoppers.

EMEA (20% spend, $57M) faced headwinds from 4% category deflation in the UK and regulatory scrutiny on HFSS (high-fat, salt, sugar) advertising, à la Nestlé's KitKat challenges. Still, we achieved 4.2x ROAS via performance marketing on Zalando and Ocado, plus influencer pods emphasizing "clean label" for our EuroFresh produce line. France and Germany saw 16% sales uplift from AR try-on filters on Snapchat, driving 25% repeat purchase intent.

APAC (10% spend, $28.5M), our growth engine, posted 4.9x ROAS amid e-comm explosion—think Tmall and Shopee mirroring Pinduoduo's CPG surge. In India, a JioMart-exclusive monsoon campaign for our SpiceEssence blends yielded 8.1x ROAS and 42% penetration lift in Tier-2 cities, leveraging vernacular TikTok content. China softened slightly to 4.3x due to zero-COVID hangover, but KOL (key opinion leader) partnerships with Douyin beauty creators boosted our skincare adjacencies by 31%.

LATAM (5% spend, $14.3M) delivered 4.0x ROAS, with Brazil's Mercado Libre sponsored search shining at 6.5x for our AguaVida beverages, countering 7% inflation via value-pack promotions.

Technically, we're ahead of the curve with several initiatives. Our in-house MMM, powered by Google's Meridian and integrated with Snowflake for real-time data lakes, now forecasts ROAS with 92% accuracy—up from 85% via legacy tools. We rolled out Clean Room tech with The Trade Desk for privacy-safe audience matching, reducing ACoS (ad cost of sale) by 22% on $120M of spend. AI personalization via Adobe Sensei optimized 15,000+ creative assets, with dynamic pricing in apps yielding 18% uplift in iOS conversion rates. And our always-on "halo" campaigns—low-funnel efficiency engines—now represent 40% of budget, stabilizing base volume like P&G's model.

Strategically, these results affirm our "Precision Growth" playbook: zero-based budgeting tied to incrementality thresholds (minimum 3.5x ROAS), 60/30/10 allocation (digital/trade/innovation), and agile pods blending media, creative, and analytics talent. Learnings include doubling down on shoppable social (TikTok Shop now 12% of digital sales) and sustainability narratives, which lifted brand equity scores by 14 points per YouGov. Risks? Rising CPMs (up 15% YoY on Meta) and signal loss, which we're mitigating with first-party data from our 45M loyalty members.

Looking ahead, Q3 marketing spend rises to $310M (up 12% YoY), targeting 5.0x+ blended ROAS. We'll scale video commerce in APAC, test connected TV in LATAM, and launch AI-generated UGC for holiday pushes. This positions us to outpace CPG peers—where industry ROAS averages 3.2x per WARC—driving 7-9% organic growth in FY24. We're also excited about the launch of our new PlantVita protein snacks, which is already generating positive feedback and strong initial sales velocity in key markets.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. The floor is now open for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, John. Happy to dive in. Our "Pure Bliss" and "Thrive Summer" campaigns were standout performers this quarter. For "Pure Bliss" on Heritage Dairy yogurt, we targeted lapsed users in the U.S. spoonable segment with a $45 million multimedia push—heavy on CTV, YouTube programmatic, Amazon and Walmart RMNs, TikTok lives, and in-store sampling. We saw a 28% household penetration lift per IRI, $165 million in incremental sales against a flat category, and 5.8x ROAS, with 65% true incrementality from geo-tests. CAC fell 18% to $4.20, improving CLV efficiency. "Thrive Summer" for plant-based snacks delivered 6.2x ROAS, 19% share gain to 14.2%, and 35% awareness bump via UGC and influencers. These drove about 1.5 points of our organic volume growth, particularly in North America where digital ROAS hit 5.1x. We're applying these learnings to Q3 with more shoppable social.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Emily. Commodity costs remain a headwind, but our hedging and productivity more than offset. We've hedged 70% of FY24 cocoa at under $4,000/ton, shielding $150 million exposure, and 50% palm oil via RSPO contracts at 1,100 MYR/ton. We assume 3-5% net YoY input inflation from cocoa in SnackJoy and palm in cleaners, but pricing delivers 5-7% realization—8% list on PowerQuench netting 6%. "MarginMax" targets $250 million savings, including $100 million from AI demand sensing and RPA in 12 plants cutting 20% conversion costs. Regenerative sourcing in Brazil avoids 5% on coffee/soy. This supports our 45.5-46.5% FY gross margin guide, with North America at 48%. Risks like El Niño are watched, but our balance sheet gives flexibility.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, David. Inflation is pressuring mass but accelerating premiumization in our portfolio. Premium now 42% of revenue, up from 32%, driving 250 bps gross margin lift to 48.7%. Health & wellness velocity up 12% in NA, AURs $3.25 vs. $2.10 mass. "PureThrive" functional water hit 18% share quickly. Our 65/35 premium/value mix insulates us—high-margin segments grow 2x category. E-com at 28% sales amplifies this, with 22% NA growth. Strategic investments in DTC and regen ag sustain momentum despite CPI at 4-5%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?

Lisa Patel:
Hi Rachel. E-commerce was a powerhouse at 28% of sales, up from 18% pre-pandemic. NA grew 22% to $1.8B, 15% grocery DTC share via Instacart/Walmart+. Europe at 20% UK household penetration. APAC exploded 45% in China to RMB 2.5B on Tmall/JD for EcoFresh. 15 DTC sites added $150M with 40% repeats. "NovaConnect" AI personalization boosts conversions 35%. Marketing ROAS 4.7x blended, with RMNs at 7.2x. Expect 4-5 points FY growth contribution, ROIC >25%. Q3 scales video commerce and connected TV.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Gross margin guidance and key assumption: Reaffirming FY2024 gross margin guidance at 45.5%-46.5% (130-180 bps expansion vs FY23 44.2%), with Q3 at 45.8% and Q4 at 46.2% midpoint. Key assumptions: 3-5% YoY input cost headwind (cocoa/palm, 70%/50% hedged), offset by 5-7% net pricing realization and $250M productivity savings (AI demand sensing, RPA, regenerative ag); North America at 48%, EMEA +100bps to 44%, EM at 42%.
aspect_summary.Summary of financial results and outlook: Q2 net sales $18.7B (+4.2% reported, +5.8% organic from 2.1% volume/mix +3.7% pricing); gross margin 53.4% (+210bps); op margin 22.1% (+140bps); adj EPS $1.42 (+11%); FCF $2.1B (11% sales). FY2024 outlook raised: organic sales 4.5-5.5% (from 4-5%), adj EPS $5.65-5.80 (+9-12% midpoint), $1.1B productivity offset by $300M investments.
aspect_summary.Marketing campaign effectiveness: Q2 marketing spend $285M (12.5% sales, +8% YoY), blended ROAS 4.7x (+24% YoY, digital 62%). Flagship: 'Pure Bliss' yogurt ($45M, 5.8x ROAS, 28% penetration lift, $165M sales uplift, 65% incremental); 'Thrive Summer' snacks ($38M, 6.2x ROAS, 19% share to 14.2%, 35% awareness). Regional ROAS: NA 5.1x, EMEA 4.2x, APAC 4.9x, LATAM 4.0x; Q3 spend $310M targeting 5.0x+ ROAS.
aspect_summary.Key strategic priorities and progress: Four priorities: (1) Premiumization/health & wellness: premium mix to 42% (+10pts in 2yrs, target 50% FY25), +250bps margins to 48.7%, e.g., PureThrive 18% share; (2) Digital/omnichannel: e-com 28% sales (+10pts), NA +22%, APAC +45%, $250M NovaConnect invest, 4-5pts growth; (3) Sustainability/supply chain: 65% recyclable packaging, 45% regen sourcing, 28% emissions cut, $180M savings; (4) Category leadership/expansion: share gains (snacks +4pts), EM +8.3% organic, new ASEAN JVs.
aspect_summary.Competitive activity and response: Aggression from P&G (Tide value packs, +1.8pts NA laundry), Unilever (Dove eco skincare), Reckitt (Dettol Europe +2.5pts), locals (HUL India -1.1pts laundry, Natura LATAM). Responses: AI pricing/promos (recaptured 1.2pts NA, +5% velocity), eco-innovations (bio-surfactants +9% Europe e-com), affordable premium packs/digital (EM +1.4pts share, +8% volume); defended 98% core share, gained in premium/EM.
